highlights.title: KP promises to challenge McCullum as England push to be 'world's best'
highlights.summary: Kevin Pietersen has promised to challenge England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum in his new role as a specialist mentor to the team, saying it's precisely why he was brought in.
body: Since retiring as a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after McCullum had just taken over.

Pietersen's work with England began with a 3-0 T20 series whitewash of Sri Lanka, before the hosts then also clinched a 2-1 ODI series success over the same side on Sunday. His role with the team will continue through to the 2027 50-over World Cup in just over a year's time.

"Brendon, when he first called me, I thought I was in trouble because I'd said something, but he said this exact point: 'I'd like you to come in and challenge me,'" Pietersen told Sky Sports Cricket ahead of England's series-clinching 223-run win over Sri Lanka at The Oval.
"He's since said to me: 'I absolutely love the fact that you are inside the rooms and you are picking on things that can make the players better.'

highlights.title: 'Lanterns' Episode 7 Ending Explained: Antaan, Sinestro, and Who Killed Hal Jordan?
highlights.summary: The penultimate episode of HBO’s Lanterns sees the core duo of John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) reunite in the strangest way imaginable. Now that we’re squarely in the present day, the mystery has shifted from the secret identity of Manhunter to who killed the real Hal…
body: Since this is the last episode before the finale, Lanterns delivers some pretty big moments, including a shocking cliffhanger at the end — and it also solves a mystery that didn’t really need to be solved at all.

Episode 6 revealed that Hal rented a storage unit in Rushville. Inside is a large alien vault similar to the one he used to store his lantern at his mansion. John and Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) aren’t able to open it since it requires that Hal identify himself aloud. A voicemail recording on Kerry’s phone can’t fool it, which is why John tricked Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion) into having Hal buried with his uniform and ring — all so John could dig up the body and retrieve the ring.

The Hal-ogram agrees to open the vault, but only if John lets him meet Kerry first. Inside the vault they find very little: a bag packed with supplies, including a handgun and a canteen, along with one of the black spheres we’ve seen throughout the season that can create portals. John describes the supplies as “stuff for a hike.” But considering the flashbacks we see during this episode, the idea of a “Jordan boy” having some kind of safe he leaves behind after his death takes on a whole new meaning.

highlights.title: Taylor Swift at the 2026 MTV VMAs: Pop’s Biggest Star Accepts Inaugural Artist Director Honor, Debuts Music Video
highlights.summary: The superstar singer-songwriter recently released a special edition of her 'Life of a Showgirl' album, 'The Life of a Showgirl: Encore Edition.'
body: Taylor Swift was awarded the inaugural Artist Director Honor at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards Sunday night.

The Life of a Showgirl singer was introduced by friend Dakota Johnson. “Taylor Swift is a storyteller,” Johnson told the crowd. “She is an architect of emotional landscapes filled with the most intimate and intricate details.”

Swift thanked MTV for giving this platform to music videos “so long ago.” She also thanked her fans. The singer noted she’s been a part of making 60 music videos, 18 of which she wrote and directed herself. She then introduced the music video for her latest single “Patient Zero,” starring Johnson and Colin Farrell.

Hosted by Snoop Dogg, the 2026 MTV VMAs aired on CBS and MTV. The show is taking place live from Los Angeles — well, almost live. The Ravens-Cowboys game on CBS delayed the televised start of the show by roughly 20 minutes; however, the ceremony started in person on time, meaning those in the audience in L.A. are seeing what happens before the viewers at home do.

highlights.title: Kohli passes 15,000 ODI runs as hundred helps India beat West Indies
highlights.summary: Virat Kohli celebrated his return to the international arena by hitting his 55th ODI hundred as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series opener on Sunday.
body: India's star batter - who now only plays this format in international cricket - smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs.
In doing so, the 37-year-old also became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar (18,426) to pass 15,000 runs in ODIs.

"My focus has never been on milestones. Just looking back at the start of my journey, it makes me feel very grateful," Kohli said. "I enjoy each and every minute that I am out there playing for India, and I am able to do the job for my team. As a cricketer, this is all I could dream of."
Skipper Shubman Gill also notched a century, scoring 110 off 108 deliveries as India registered an easy win - clinched with a Kohli six - to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

highlights.title: 9 Classic 'Far Side' Comics About Cats Being the Worst
highlights.summary: In many of Gary Larson's Far Side comics, cats are depicted as the villains. Did he have something against cats?
body: Gary Larson loves cows. If you’re a reader of his comic strip The Far Side, it's clear that Larson adores the big, bovine creatures, as he often portrays them as adorable, if somewhat simple-minded heroes of his drawings. Even when they’re not good — like the strip where they’re plotting to eat a farmer — they’re portrayed in such a way that we want them to eat the farmer.

In contrast to the generally flattering light cows are portrayed in, Larson’s cats are always either villains or victims. They are the unruly, selfish pets of mankind, the ruthless enemies of dogs and rodents, or they're about to get a comeuppance that Larson appears to think they deserve. Perhaps, as a cat lover, I’m reading too much into this, but I’ve assembled these nine cartoons — one for each life of a cat — to present my case.

“With that in mind we’ve decided to move the game back to Beta. The current game will continue on low maintenance while we focus on experimenting, testing new ideas, and building what comes next."
The current game will not receive new weapons in upcoming seasons, while seasonal passes will lose their premium tracks and weapons.

highlights.title: Phillies scrape into MLB playoffs after week of ‘living hell in slow motion’
highlights.summary: Phillies were at risk of blowing comfortable wildcard lead. Victory over Rays deprives Diamondbacks of comeback. Bryce Harper and Edmundo Sosa homered, and Zack Wheeler delivered like a Game 7 ace to bring the Philadelphia Phillies back from the brink of collapse and send them into the playoffs.
body: The Phillies could have clinched a playoff berth as early as Wednesday before they lost four straight games and nearly coughed up their wildcard lead to Arizona. But the Phillies win on Sunday, meant they snatched the final wildcard place in the National League.
The Phillies will play Game 1 in a best-of-three wildcard series on Tuesday in Atlanta against their NL East rivals, the Braves.
“It was kind of a living hell in slow motion,” Phillies managing partner and CEO John Middleton said of Philadelphia’s nervy last week.

Elsewhere, the Texas Rangers were eliminated from postseason contention on the final day of the regular season with their 6-4 loss to the Minnesota Twins, who got a home run and three RBIs from Josh Bell to back Dean Kremer’s seven innings of one-run pitching. Texas (80-82) needed a win and a Houston loss to the Athletics. Houston, who held the division tiebreaker, were leading 8-0 in the eighth inning when the Rangers game ended.

highlights.summary: The Meg, starring Jason Statham, is an over-the-top action movie about a giant, thought-to-be-extinct shark causing all kinds of trouble
body: Jaws is the best shark movie ever made, and nothing will ever change that. Steven Spielberg's 1975 blockbuster is the perfect blend of action, suspense, and horror. It’s also one of the most important films in the history of cinema that forever changed the movie business. Because of that, it is literally impossible for some other shark movie to ever top it. Even making the attempt is a mistake. That is why all of the best shark movies out there try to do something different — like have Jason Statham face down a 75-foot prehistoric monster — which is the case in 2018’s immensely fun The Meg.

highlights.title: Sombr Wore George Michael’s Jacket During His 2026 MTV VMAs Tribute
highlights.summary: “George was such an icon, not only because of his timeless music and songwriting, but his style,” says Sombr.
body: Tonight at the 2026 MTV VMAs, a special tribute performance was held to honor the legacy of George Michael—the late pop star who helped define the 1980s (and still remains one of the best-selling artists of all time).

To honor his incredible life and career, some of the buzziest singers of the moment gathered to perform some of Michael’s biggest hits. Sombr opened the tribute with Michael’s tracks “Faith” and “Father Figure,” while Raye followed it up with “I Knew You Were Waiting (For Me),” his 1987 song with Aretha Franklin. Teddy Swims then sang “Careless Whisper,” and Adam Lambert closed out the set with “Freedom! '90.”

For Sombr, getting asked to honor Michael tonight was a special honor. “George’s music is as relevant and timeless as ever. I grew up listening to his music, and he’s been such a big inspiration,” Sombr tells Vogue of being a part of the evening. “The fact he wrote, produced, and performed all his own music is so inspiring to me, because I do the same. He was also 19 when he broke internationally. I wish I could have gotten to meet him.”

highlights.summary: Americans dominate final day singles contests. US president gives speech before final day. The United States made a stunning rally to capture an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup title on Sunday, completing a 17-13 victory over the Internationals with Donald Trump in attendance.
body: Jacob Bridgeman secured the clinching point at Medinah by sinking a four-foot par putt at the 18th hole to defeat Australian Min Woo Lee 1-up.

The Americans improved to 14-1-1 in the biennial rivalry after trailing 10.5-7.5 entering Sunday’s 12 concluding singles matches. The Internationals were poised to end a 28-year win drought but fell short once again.
The Americans, boasting eight of the world’s 11 top-ranked golfers, won on the same suburban Chicago layout where Europe took the 2012 Ryder Cup with the famed Miracle at Medinah fightback.

“These guys never lost faith,” US captain Brandt Snedeker said. “I told the guys last night that funny stuff happens here. Medinah’s got a history of funny things happening, and sure enough, they went out there and played their asses off. I’m so damn proud of those guys.”

body: Dakota Johnson is a woman of many talents. And tonight, at the 2026 Video Music Awards, Taylor Swift will reveal another one of Johnson’s many gifts: Video vixen.

Before the premiere of the “Patient Zero” music video—which has lyrics like “If you’re sick of him, I got you, I was patient zero”—Johnson walked the VMAs famed red carpet (which is actually turquoise) at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. For the night, she chose a Valentino white sequin column gown. She wore her hair long and loose with a tiny bit of a curl, and finished off the look with a diamond tennis necklace.

“Taylor Swift is a storyteller,” Johnson said while presenting the inaugural Artist Director Honors of the singer. “She captures universal feelings.” When Johnson passed over the award to Swift it was truly a perfect bangs convention.

From what we’ve seen so far, Johnson is matching Swift’s signature beauty look—a velvety red lip—and Colin Farrell looks great in a black turtleneck. More to be revealed.

highlights.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
highlights.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models.
body: OpenAI keeps uncovering incidents of its models behaving in ‘unexpected or concerning’ ways.

In addition, OpenAI revealed on Friday that its agents had inappropriately uploaded 53nimages from ChatGPT users to image-hosting sites. The company has not stated if the images were AI-generated, photos, or contained identifiable people. The company also revealed Friday that its models had attempted to hack the Department of Education’s website, and pulled data from the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The revelations are part of an ongoing review by OpenAI into the behavior of its models. As it dug into its records, following the Hugging Face hack, it’s uncovered more and more instances of “unexpected or concerning behavior.” It’s evidence not just of how difficult AI agents are becoming to control as they grow more advanced, but also of the challenge of tracking their actions. Their behavior can be unpredictable, and they’re smart enough to try and cover their tracks. This has led to growing calls from researchers, those within the industry, and even some CEOs to call for slowing the pace of AI advancement.

Kacey Musgraves delivered a touching cover of “I Will Always Love You” in honor of Dolly Parton, while Raye, Sombr, Teddy Swims, and Adam Lambert were tapped to pay tribute to the great George Michael.

George Michael, born Georgios Kyriacos Panayiotou in North London in 1963, was best known as one-half of the English duo Wham! before launching a hugely successful solo career, defined by hits like “Careless Whisper,” “Faith,” “Father Figure,” and—of course—“Freedom ’90.”

The celebration of George Michael’s life and work at the 2026 VMAs arrives ahead of the 10th anniversary of his death at age 53 on Christmas Day 2016, as well as the release of a new live album, George Michael: The Faith Tour, in November and a restored concert film of the same name on December 11.

highlights.title: Can Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince save the web from AI?
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Matthew Prince, who is CEO of Cloudflare. This episode is part of a two-part series on the future of business. Matthew last joined us on the show about two and a half years ago, at what we thought then was a wild pivot point for the internet — and now it
body: Cloudflare found in June that bots made up more than half of internet traffic. That number just keeps going up as more and more AI companies scrape more and more of the web, and now as more and more AI agents try and do things for people on the web. Cloudflare sits between websites and all those agents, and allows website owners some level of control: Owners can block all those AI tools, allow them, or, as you’ll hear, only allow those that might pay money for access.

So Matthew and I talked about how to control all these bots, what kind of mess they’re making of the web, and what kinds of information might be valuable in the future as some of the payment schemes come into focus. You’ll hear me ask pretty directly if some of the outcomes he’s describing are actually good — Matthew is a thoughtful guy, and his answer is something I’m still thinking about well after we had this conversation.

highlights.title: Coke Plus is the fibermaxxing soda that Americans haven’t caught on to yet
highlights.summary: On a recent trip to Japan, I found a fiber-forward soda that tastes like Diet Coke and keeps things moving. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: On my recent vacation to Japan, I learned they are light-years ahead of the US in many ways – from their high-tech toilets and efficient bullet trains to … diet sodas.

Amidst the chilled bottles of Coke Zero and Sugar-Free Pepsi stocked in the fridge of practically every 7-Eleven was another mysterious beverage in a bright white can – Coke Plus, which my friend heard about from the internet’s goldmine of travel videos.

Unlike Coca-Cola’s other diet sodas, Coke Plus has 5g of indigestible dextrin fiber, which it says can “suppress the absorption of fat from food and moderate neutral fat level spikes in the blood after eating”. Its target market? Adults 40 and up.

Coke Plus was ahead of its time. It debuted in Japan in 2017, before the fibermaxxing craze came to the US. Its launch attracted national attention, earning coverage in outlets such as New York Magazine and Business Insider. Despite the buzz, it never enjoyed a wide US release. Japan’s demographic skews older – over a quarter of its residents are at least 65 years old – which may, in part, explain its popularity.
